query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Find relevant Java backend and Spring Boot jobs, build or retrieve tailored resume documents, and email job alerts or applications through Gmail.
query_ground_truth.query: look up newly posted employment opportunities for Spring Boot and Java backend engineers
query_ground_truth.rationale: To discover current job listings for Java backend and Spring Boot roles, a web search tool is directly required.

request.query: look up newly posted employment opportunities for Spring Boot and Java backend engineers

results.use_case: look up newly posted employment opportunities for Spring Boot and Java backend engineers
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if location/region inputs are unclear)] [Prerequisite]: Validate acceptable location strings using SERPAPI_GET_AVAILABLE_LOCATION_OPTIONS_FOR_GOOGLE_SEARCHES (avoid invalid or overly narrow values).
[Optional (if a region-specific domain is needed)] [Prerequisite]: Select an appropriate domain using SERPAPI_GOOGLE_DOMAINS_LIST (align localization expectations).
[Required] [Step 1]: Search for live job postings using SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH (use the provided query; capture jobs_results and any available application links).
[Required (if results are empty)] [Step 2]: Relax constraints and re-run SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH (remove strict filters/terms to restore coverage).
[Optional (if more than one page is needed)] [Next Step]: Paginate SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH using next_page_token until no token is returned; merge results.
[Required (if the jobs vertical remains empty or unavailable)] [Fallback]: Run a broader discovery query using SERPAPI_SEARCH (identify relevant posting pages from organic results).
[Optional (if source trust is unclear)] [Next Step]: Vet a small subset of shortlisted results using SERPAPI_GET_GOOGLE_ABOUT_THIS_RESULT (deprioritize low-quality sources).
known_pitfalls: [SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH] May return an empty-state indicator (e.g., jobs_results_state or error fields) despite a successful call; treat as no-results rather than a hard failure.
[SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH] next_page_token is the only pagination signal; missing token means end-of-results (not an error).
[SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH] status_code 401 indicates invalid credentials; fix credentials before assuming the query/location is wrong.
[SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH] Optional filters/fields may appear under detected_extensions and can be absent; don’t assume salary/posted metadata exists.
[SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH] apply_options is an array; don’t assume a single apply URL is always present.

toolkit_connection_statuses.description: SerpApi provides a real-time API for structured search engine results, allowing developers to scrape, parse, and analyze SERP data for SEO and research
toolkit_connection_statuses.status_message: No Active connection for toolkit=serpapi. You MUST call COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS (toolkit="serpapi") to create a connection BEFORE executing any serpapi tools.

SERPAPI_GOOGLE_JOBS_SEARCH.description: Retrieve Google Jobs Search Results via SerpApi. Returns job SERP data in JSON; key attributes like `work_from_home`, `posted_at`, `salary`, and `schedule_type` are nested under `detected_extensions` per job object and are often absent — treat as optional. Results may include stale postings; verify recency via `detected_extensions.posted_at`. Supports pagination, location filtering, and remote-job filtering.

q.description: Parameter defines the query you want to search.

gl.description: Parameter defines the country to use for the Google search. It's a two-letter country code.

hl.description: Parameter defines the language to use for the Google Jobs search. It's a two-letter language code.

uds.description: Parameter enables to filter search. It's a string provided by Google as a filter.

lrad.description: Defines search radius in kilometers. Does not strictly limit the radius.

uule.description: Parameter is the Google encoded location you want to use for the search. uule and location parameters can't be used together. Note: the resolved `location_used` in the response may differ from `location_requested`.

chips.description: Parameter defines additional query conditions. Top of a job search page contains elements called chips, its values are extracted in order to be passed to chips parameter.

ltype.description: Parameter will filter the results by work from home. Set to 1 for work from home jobs.

engine.description: Set parameter to google_jobs to use the Google Jobs API engine.

output.description: Parameter defines the final output you want. It can be set to json (default) to get a structured JSON of the results, or html to get the raw html retrieved.

examples: new york, new york, united states
location.description: Parameter defines from where you want the search to originate. If several locations match the location requested, we'll pick the most popular one. It is recommended to specify location at the city level in order to simulate a real user’s search.

no_cache.description: Parameter will force SerpApi to fetch the Google Jobs results even if a cached version is already present.

async_req.description: Parameter defines the way you want to submit your search to SerpApi.

zero_trace.description: Enterprise only. Parameter enables ZeroTrace mode. It can be set to false (default) or true.

google_domain.description: Parameter defines the Google domain to use. It defaults to google.com.

next_page_token.description: Parameter defines the next page token. It is used for retrieving the next page of results. Up to 10 results are returned per page.

SERPAPI_GET_AVAILABLE_LOCATION_OPTIONS_F.description: Tool to get available location options for Google searches. Returns location names, codes, and identifiers that can be used in the location parameter. Use when you need to find valid location values for search queries.

q.description: Restricts your search to locations that contain the supplied string. For example, 'Austin' will find 'Austin, TX', 'The University of Texas at Austin', etc. If not provided, returns general location options.

limit.description: Limits the number of locations returned. Must be between 1 and 10. If not specified, returns all matching locations up to the maximum of 10.

SERPAPI_GOOGLE_DOMAINS_LIST.description: Retrieve the list of supported Google domains for search queries.
